start_gpsd.description: Whether to automatically start the gpsd daemon on system boot.

devices.description: List of serial device paths (e.g., USB GPS dongles) or network endpoints (e.g., 'localhost:2947') to monitor.

items.description: A valid device path (e.g., /dev/ttyUSB0) or network endpoint.

serial_options.description: Serial port settings in 'baud,parity,stop' format (e.g., '9600,8,N,1'). If empty, gpsd auto-detects.

gpsd_options.description: Additional daemon flags. '-n' enables immediate polling of devices on startup; '-b' enables Bluetooth support.

output_format.description: Default output format for clients that don’t request a specific format. Common: 'json' (default), 'nmea', or 'aivdm'. Leave blank to use built-in default.

user.description: System user account under which gpsd runs. Use a dedicated non-root user for security.

group.description: System group for gpsd’s runtime permissions. Usually matches the user group.

socket.description: Unix domain socket path used for client communication. Change only for special deployments (e.g., chroot).

pps_enable.description: Enable pulse-per-second (PPS) input for high-precision time discipline (e.g., with NTP/chrony). Requires compatible hardware.

shm_enable.description: Export GPS time data via shared memory for low-latency clients (e.g., chrony using shm://0).

allowed_clients.description: Comma-separated list of trusted client types allowed to connect (e.g., 'ntp,chrony'). Empty allows all.
